name: nordic-fish

description.en: 55 fish species of Swedish and Nordic fresh and coastal waters: salmon and trout, pike, perch and zander, carp-like fishes, cod fishes, herring and sprat, flatfish, a shark, a ray, a lamprey and others. Front: the English and the Swedish name; back: the scientific name. Scientific and Swedish names follow Dyntaxa (SLU Artdatabanken), English names Wikidata (one from Dyntaxa). Data from Wikidata and Dyntaxa, checked against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes and FishBase.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (scripted lookups in Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes and FishBase, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Scope and authority. The library editor asked for about 50 fish species of Swedish and Nordic fresh and coastal waters, the common name (English and Swedish) on the front and the scientific name on the back, with one stated authority for accepted names. Dyntaxa, the Swedish taxonomic database of SLU Artdatabanken, published on GBIF under CC0 (dataset publication date 2026-09-29), was chosen as the single authority for both the scientific names and the Swedish names, so that the two always refer to the same taxon concept. Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (online version updated 21 Sep. 2026) and FishBase (version 06/2026) were used to verify, not as sources of card content, because neither allows reuse in an open deck.

Candidate list. The authoring agent wrote down 126 candidate names from general knowledge of the Nordic fish fauna (salmonids and whitefish, pike, perch and other percids, carp-like fishes, catfish, sculpins, sticklebacks, loaches, lampreys, cod fishes, herrings, mackerels, flatfish, sharks, rays and other marine fishes), including older or alternative names (for example Stizostedion lucioperca, Aspius aspius, Psetta maxima, Abramis ballerus, Triglopsis quadricornis, Coregonus lavaretus, Salvelinus umbla) to see how the sources treat them. No published list was copied.

Dyntaxa (content source and authority). Each candidate name was looked up in the Dyntaxa checklist on GBIF (species search restricted to the dataset, exact canonical name); for every matching record its vernacular names (with GBIF's 'preferred' flag, which marks Dyntaxa's recommended Swedish name), and for accepted records its synonyms and its Swedish distribution record (status, establishment means, threat status) were fetched (script dyntaxa.py, queries below). Where a name was a Dyntaxa synonym, the accepted name was looked up as well (Gymnocephalus cernuus for Gymnocephalus cernua); Platichthys solemdali was looked up after the flounder's record showed a split. A Dyntaxa evidence locator on a card names the GBIF species record (https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/<key>); what its 'says' reports comes from that record and its sub-endpoints /vernacularNames (the Swedish names and the preferred flag), /synonyms and /distributions (status and establishment means in Sweden), which the script fetched.

Wikidata (content source). One SPARQL query (the first query below) fetched, for every candidate name (and Gymnocephalus cernuus, Dyntaxa's accepted name for the ruffe), the items with that taxon name (P225), their rank, English and Swedish labels and aliases, Dyntaxa ID (P1939) and the names of their taxon synonyms (P1420). A second query did the same for the final names plus the two older names whose Wikidata items carry the labels (Aspius aspius, Gymnocephalus cernua). Further queries fetched the taxon-synonym links between paired items, the Baltic herring item and the Platichthys solemdali item.

Selection. The candidates were filtered by the criteria in the selection section and cut by editorial judgement to the species best known to Nordic anglers, fish buyers and naturalists; exclusions and reasons are listed there.

Card text. Back: Dyntaxa's accepted scientific name, tagged as Latin; for every card it is also the taxon name (P225) of a Wikidata item. Swedish front: Dyntaxa's preferred Swedish vernacular name, exactly as Dyntaxa writes it (lower case). English front: an English label or alias of the species' Wikidata item, chosen by these rules: (a) the item's English label when it is a common name of the species (39 cards, including the three-spined stickleback after review round 3); (b) where the label is also a name of a wider group or another species, or a longer form, the alias that is FishBase's main English name: northern pike (label 'pike', also the genus Esox), saithe (label 'pollock', close to 'Atlantic pollock', Wikidata's name for the pollack) and rudd (label 'common rudd'); (c) where the label is the scientific name, the alias that is FishBase's main English name (vendace, roach, common carp, gudgeon, Atlantic cod, Atlantic herring, European plaice, Atlantic halibut, lumpfish, round goby), except where the compiler chose another alias: brown trout (FishBase 'Sea trout', which also names the sea-run form) and monkfish (FishBase 'Angler', not a Wikidata name; 'monkfish' is the trade name, with 'anglerfish' in the note). Fronts are written in lower case except proper nouns and words derived from them (Atlantic, Arctic, European); for the spurdog Wikidata has no such name ('spiny dogfish shark', alias 'Spiny dogfish') and the card uses Dyntaxa's English name 'Spurdog'. Where Wikidata has two items for one species (the ruffe and the asp), the label check is on the item with the labels and the taxon-name check on the item with Dyntaxa's name. No Swedish front was translated by the agent; the Swedish notes were written by the agent.

Notes. Back notes give former scientific names where the change is recent enough to be met in books and on menus (zander: Stizostedion; asp: Aspius; turbot: Psetta), each supported by a Wikidata taxon-synonym link (P1420) and, for the asp and the turbot, Dyntaxa's synonyms; the ruffe's other spelling (Gymnocephalus cernua, used by the Catalog of Fishes and FishBase, the taxon name of Wikidata's labelled item, listed by Dyntaxa as a synonym); other Swedish names from Dyntaxa's non-preferred names and Wikidata's Swedish labels and aliases (fjällröding, bergtunga, sjötunga, horngädda); other English names from Wikidata's aliases (coalfish, lumpsucker, spiny dogfish, anglerfish); the Swedish name of Baltic herring (Wikidata item Q10826808, Clupea harengus membras: en 'Baltic herring', sv 'strömming'; Dyntaxa lists 'strömming' as another Swedish name of Clupea harengus; the note's 'most of the Baltic' was checked against Swedish Wikipedia's article Sill, verification only); for the flounder, the Baltic flounder Platichthys solemdali described in 2018 (English name from Wikidata's alias of Q55713149), which Dyntaxa accepts and to which it also gives 'skrubbskädda' as another Swedish name, so the flounder card has a front note that narrows the front; and, for the bleak and the vendace, that Dyntaxa gives 'löja' to both (preferred for the bleak, another name of the vendace). The note 'Non-native in Sweden.' / 'Främmande art i Sverige.' marks the three species whose Dyntaxa distribution record has establishment means INTRODUCED (brook trout, common carp, round goby); FishBase's distribution text (verification) gives their native ranges in North America and the Black, Caspian and Aral Sea basins.

Verification with Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes. For every card the Catalog's species query (fishcatget.asp?tbl=species&genus=…&species=…) was fetched and its 'Current status' lines extracted (script cof.py): every scientific name on the cards is 'Valid as' that name, except the ruffe, which the Catalog spells Gymnocephalus cernua (see quality control). The pages of the older names were fetched too.

Verification with FishBase. For every card the FishBase species summary page and its common-names list were fetched (scripts fishbase.py and fbnames.py). Every English front is among FishBase's English common names of the species and every Swedish front among its Swedish common names; FishBase's main English name differs from the card's for 10 cards (recorded in quality control).

Ambiguity check. A SPARQL query (<scratch>/ambig.rq, posted by <scratch>/ambig.py; below) looked for every Wikidata taxon carrying a card's English or Swedish front (in lower case, capitalised or title case) as a label or alias. The script fbnames.py also checked whether FishBase gives a card's English name for another species in the deck. After review, the script <scratch>/qc1/svambig.py checked every card's Swedish front against all Swedish names (preferred and other) of the other deck species' Dyntaxa records and Platichthys solemdali: 'löja' (also the vendace) and 'skrubbskädda' (also Platichthys solemdali) are shared, and both cards say so. When review round 3 changed the stickleback front to 'three-spined stickleback', the query was re-run for that front (<scratch>/qc4/ambig4.rq): it matches only Gasterosteus aculeatus and its nominate subspecies G. a. aculeatus. The findings are under quality control; apart from the flounder's front (given a front note), none was judged to make a front ambiguous in a deck of Nordic fish.

Machine checks. Every card has a Wikidata check of the taxon name (P225); 54 cards also check that the item's Dyntaxa ID (P1939) is the Dyntaxa taxon used, and cards check their English and Swedish fronts as a label or alias wherever Wikidata has that text in exactly the card's letter case (45 English and 40 Swedish fronts). The notes are checked where they rest on Wikidata (taxon synonyms, aliases, the Baltic herring and Platichthys solemdali items). The builder runs all checks against live Wikidata on every build.
selection: The deck has 55 fish species of Swedish and Nordic waters: 31 of fresh water or that spawn in it (6 salmonids, smelt, pike, 3 percids, burbot, eel, 11 carp-like fishes, wels catfish, bullhead, 2 sticklebacks, 2 loaches and the river lamprey) and 24 of the sea and coast (5 cod fishes, herring, sprat, Atlantic mackerel, Atlantic horse mackerel, garfish, 7 flatfish, lumpfish, eelpout, wolffish, monkfish, spurdog, thornback ray and round goby). Inclusion criteria: (1) an accepted taxon in Dyntaxa with a preferred Swedish vernacular name; (2) Dyntaxa's distribution status in Sweden PRESENT (native, or introduced and established); (3) a Wikidata item with Dyntaxa's name as taxon name and an English name of the species in its labels or aliases (or, for the spurdog, in Dyntaxa); (4) 'Valid as' in Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (the ruffe in its other spelling); (5) familiarity to a Nordic beginner, which decided the final cut. Introduced species are included when Dyntaxa lists them as present: brook trout, common carp and round goby. Left out after research: the whitefish (sik), because the species concept is unsettled: Dyntaxa's 'sik' is Coregonus maraena and it marks Coregonus lavaretus as absent from Sweden, while Wikidata's item labelled 'sik' is Coregonus lavaretus and its Coregonus maraena item is labelled 'Älvsik', so the card would have no one right answer across sources; rainbow trout (regnbåge), Atlantic bluefin tuna (blåfenad tonfisk), capelin (lodda), basking shark and others whose Dyntaxa status in Sweden is IRREGULAR; Greenland halibut and Coregonus lavaretus (ABSENT); the pollack (lyrtorsk), because Wikidata's only English name for it is 'Atlantic pollock', easily confused with the saithe's American name; the European hake, whose Wikidata items are split (one has the Swedish label, another the English); the shorthorn sculpin (rötsimpa), which has no English name in Wikidata; and white bream, common dace, vimba, fourhorn sculpin, brill, greater weever, black goby, ballan wrasse, Prussian carp, the brook and sea lampreys and other marine species, only to keep the deck near the requested size. Taxonomy follows Dyntaxa throughout: Leuciscus aspius (not Aspius aspius), Sander lucioperca (not Stizostedion), Scophthalmus maximus (not Psetta maxima), Gymnocephalus cernuus (the Catalog of Fishes and FishBase: Gymnocephalus cernua), and Platichthys flesus in the narrow sense, without the Baltic flounder Platichthys solemdali. Subspecies and forms (sea trout, Baltic herring) are not separate cards.

rounds.lens: Sources and machine checks: every card's scientific, English and Swedish names compared across Dyntaxa (GBIF), Wikidata, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes and FishBase; fronts checked for ambiguity against Wikidata taxa and FishBase's names of the other deck species.
rounds.scope: All 55 cards and the candidates left out.
rounds.summary: All 55 scientific names are Dyntaxa's accepted names and the taxon name (P225) of a Wikidata item; 54 of those items have Dyntaxa's taxon as their Dyntaxa ID. The Catalog of Fishes gives every name as valid except the ruffe's spelling. Every English and Swedish front is among FishBase's common names of the species. Wikidata differs from the cards in letter case or in the name chosen for 10 English and 15 Swedish fronts: those label checks are left out and recorded below.

findings.issue: Wikidata has the card's English name only in another letter case for 9 cards: northern-pike (Q165278: label 'pike', alias 'Northern pike'); burbot (Q144700: 'Burbot'); roach (Q182976: alias 'Roach'); crucian-carp (Q194031: 'Crucian carp'); gudgeon (Q237619: alias 'Gudgeon'); common-ling (Q842406: 'Common ling'); garfish (Q643373: 'Garfish'); viviparous-eelpout (Q27336: 'Viviparous eelpout'); round-goby (Q838199: alias 'Round goby').
findings.resolution: The cards keep the deck's convention (lower case except proper nouns); the English label check is left out for these cards (the taxon-name and Dyntaxa-ID checks still run).

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish label differs from Dyntaxa's preferred name only in letter case for 11 cards: european-smelt ('Nors'), burbot ('Lake'), rudd ('Sarv'), crucian-carp ('Ruda'), wels-catfish ('Mal'), stone-loach ('Grönling'), spined-loach ('Nissöga'), common-ling ('Långa'), turbot ('Piggvar'), thornback-ray ('Knaggrocka'), round-goby ('Svartmunnad smörbult').
findings.resolution: Dyntaxa writes Swedish animal names in lower case; the cards keep Dyntaxa's form and the Swedish label check is left out.

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish label is another name than Dyntaxa's preferred name for 4 cards: atlantic-salmon (Q188879: 'atlantlax', card 'lax'); arctic-char (Q421047: 'fjällröding', card 'röding'); common-sole (Q27773: 'sjötunga', card 'tunga'); lemon-sole (Q127463: 'bergtunga', card 'bergskädda').
findings.resolution: The cards follow Dyntaxa, the stated authority for Swedish names; FishBase lists both names in each case. Fjällröding, sjötunga and bergtunga are given in back notes (checked as Wikidata labels); 'atlantlax' is not, as Dyntaxa does not list it.

findings.issue: Wikidata has no English label or alias 'spurdog' for Squalus acanthias (label 'spiny dogfish shark', aliases 'Spiny dogfish', 'Squalus acanthias'); FishBase's main English name is 'Piked dogfish'.
findings.resolution: The card uses Dyntaxa's English name 'Spurdog' (lower case), the usual name in Britain and Ireland (FishBase lists it there); 'spiny dogfish' is in the back note and checked as a Wikidata alias.

findings.issue: Dyntaxa's accepted name is Gymnocephalus cernuus (with Gymnocephalus cernua as a synonym); Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes and FishBase use Gymnocephalus cernua ('The name cernua is a noun [as described by Linnaeus with a capital C]'). Wikidata has two items with no statement linking them: Q187981 (Gymnocephalus cernua, with the labels) and Q50407492 (Gymnocephalus cernuus, with the Dyntaxa ID).
findings.resolution: The card follows the stated authority, Dyntaxa, and its back note says the name is often spelled Gymnocephalus cernua; P225 and P1939 are checked on Q50407492, the labels and the spelling cernua on Q187981. The tie between the two items rests on Dyntaxa's synonym list.

findings.issue: Wikidata's labels 'asp'/'asp' are on Q182894 (Aspius aspius); the item with Dyntaxa's name Leuciscus aspius, Q25473019, has the Dyntaxa ID and the Swedish label 'Asp (fisk)'.
findings.resolution: P225 and P1939 are checked on Q25473019, the labels on Q182894, and the taxon-synonym link Q25473019 → Q182894 (P1420) is checked so the two checks refer to one species; back note 'Formerly Aspius aspius.'

findings.issue: Dyntaxa's record of Platichthys flesus is a new taxon (6039902) with the synonym 'Platichthys flesus (Linnaeus, 1758) s.str.', next to the Baltic flounder Platichthys solemdali Momigliano et al., 2018 (taxon 6039901, 'östersjöskrubbskädda'), to which Dyntaxa also gives 'skrubbskädda' as another Swedish name. Wikidata's Dyntaxa ID for Q214034 is still '206209'.
findings.resolution: The card means Platichthys flesus in Dyntaxa's sense, with its preferred name 'skrubbskädda'; a back note names Platichthys solemdali so that learners do not take the Baltic species for it. No P1939 check on this card; P225 of Q214034 and Q55713149 (Platichthys solemdali) are checked.

findings.issue: Whitefish: Dyntaxa's 'sik' is Coregonus maraena (Coregonus lavaretus misapplied; Coregonus lavaretus 'lavaretsik' ABSENT in Sweden), while Wikidata's 'sik' label is on Coregonus lavaretus (Q743084, with 'Coregonus maraena' as a Swedish alias) and Coregonus maraena (Q1034400) is labelled 'Älvsik' with only the English alias 'Maraene'.
findings.resolution: Left out: the card would not have one right scientific name across sources, and no English name for Coregonus maraena is in a content source. Recorded in the selection.

findings.issue: Ambiguity query: some fronts are also Wikidata names of other taxa: 'grayling' (also Hipparchia semele, a butterfly), 'roach' (Blattodea; the genus Rutilus; Semotilus bullaris), 'asp' (sv: also Populus tremula, Vipera species), 'mal' (sv: also Tineoidea), 'tunga' (the flea genus Tunga), 'sill' (also the genus Clupea), 'flodnejonöga' (also Petromyzontiformes), 'garfish' (also Belonidae), 'brook trout' (also an alias of Oncorhynchus mykiss), 'vendace' (also Coregonus vandesius), 'bleak' (also Alburnoides bipunctatus), 'whiting' (also Brevoortia tyrannus). rounds.scope: All 55 cards, re-checked against WoRMS and Dyntaxa (via GBIF) queried independently, and all 211 Wikidata checks.
rounds.summary: No card was found wrong; every scientific name is accepted in Dyntaxa and WoRMS (except the ruffe's spelling), every Swedish front is Dyntaxa's preferred name, and the counts and non-native notes are right. Three warnings (the ruffe note, 'skrubbskädda' shared with Platichthys solemdali, 'löja' shared with the vendace) and three suggestions. All six were verified against live sources and all but part of the monkfish suggestion applied.

findings.issue: The back note 'Often spelled Gymnocephalus cernua.' makes the spelling used by the Catalog of Fishes, FishBase and WoRMS (which marks Gymnocephalus cernuus 'unaccepted') sound like a mere variant.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: WoRMS AphiaRecordsByName for Gymnocephalus cernuus gives status 'unaccepted', valid_name 'Gymnocephalus cernua'. The note now names the convention: 'Dyntaxa's spelling; the Catalog of Fishes and FishBase write Gymnocephalus cernua.' / 'Dyntaxas stavning; Catalog of Fishes och FishBase skriver Gymnocephalus cernua.' (both are already in the card's evidence; WoRMS was not added as a source).

findings.issue: The Swedish front 'skrubbskädda' is also a Dyntaxa name of Platichthys solemdali, and the back note only shows after answering.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (GBIF 253514641/vernacularNames: 'östersjöskrubbskädda' preferred, 'skrubbskädda' not preferred). Added a front note 'in the narrow sense, not the Baltic flounder' / 'i snäv mening, inte östersjöskrubbskädda', and the English back note now gives the English name Baltic flounder (Wikidata alias of Q55713149, now checked).

findings.issue: The Swedish front 'löja' is also a Dyntaxa name of the vendace (Coregonus albula), another card; the ambiguity check did not cover Dyntaxa's non-preferred names.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (GBIF 159941928/vernacularNames: 'siklöja' preferred, 'löja', 'vimma'). Back notes added: bleak 'Swedish löja can also mean the vendace (siklöja).' / 'Löja kan också syfta på siklöja.'; vendace 'Also called löja in Swedish.' / 'Kallas också löja.' The ambiguity check was extended (script <scratch>/qc1/svambig.py): of all Swedish fronts, only 'löja' and 'skrubbskädda' are Dyntaxa names of another deck species or of P. solemdali. The regional claim (northern Sweden, löjrom) was left out, as the deck's sources do not state it.

findings.issue: The note 'Baltic herring is called strömming in Swedish.' oversimplifies: herring from the southern Baltic is called sill.
findings.resolution: Confirmed in Swedish Wikipedia's article Sill ('Traditionellt har namnet strömming använts för sill fångad i större delen av Östersjön'), added as a verification source. Note now: 'Herring from most of the Baltic is called strömming in Swedish.' / 'Sill från större delen av Östersjön kallas strömming.' The exact boundary (Kristianopel or Kalmar Sound, given as alternatives) was left out.

findings.issue: 'monkfish' is also a WoRMS English name of the angelshark (Squatina squatina) and Lophius americanus.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (WoRMS AphiaRecordsByVernacular/monkfish returns Lophius americanus, Lophius piscatorius, Squatina squatina). Recorded here: in a deck of Nordic fish 'monkfish' names Lophius piscatorius (Wikidata alias, the trade name); Lophius americanus is not Nordic, and the angelshark is not in the deck. The suggested 'angler' in the note was not added, because it is not a name in the deck's content sources (Wikidata has 'Anglerfish' and 'monkfish'; FishBase is verification only).

findings.issue: The selection counts '2 mackerels' though the horse mackerel is a jack (Carangidae); the description says 'English names Wikidata' though the spurdog's comes from Dyntaxa.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (WoRMS classification of 126822: Carangiformes, Carangidae). Selection now says 'Atlantic mackerel, Atlantic horse mackerel'; the description says 'English names Wikidata (one from Dyntaxa)' / 'engelska namn Wikidata (ett från Dyntaxa)'.

rounds.summary: Licensing is sound (Wikidata and Dyntaxa CC0 content; Catalog of Fishes and FishBase verification only). One warning: the stated rule for English fronts ('the one most used in Europe') could not be reproduced and was not followed for 'threespine stickleback'. findings.issue: The method's rule 'the one most used in Europe' names no source and was not followed: the card used the North American 'threespine stickleback' instead of the Wikidata label and FishBase main name 'three-spined stickleback'; northern-pike and ninespine-stickleback also rest on judgement.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (Wikidata Q203572: label 'three-spined stickleback', alias 'threespine stickleback'; FishBase page title 'Three-spined stickleback'). The front is now 'three-spined stickleback' (label check updated). The method's rule was replaced with the rule actually applied, checked card by card against the Wikidata labels (script <scratch>/qc1/enlabels.py): the label when it is a common name of the species; otherwise the alias that is FishBase's main name, with the judgement cases named (northern pike, saithe, rudd, brown trout, monkfish, spurdog). 'ninespine stickleback' stays: it is both Wikidata's label and FishBase's main name, and Wikidata has no 'nine-spined' form.

The query was re-run today for 'three-spined stickleback', 'Three-spined stickleback', 'Three-spined Stickleback' and 'Three-Spined Stickleback' (<scratch>/qc4/ambig4.rq, recorded under queries). rounds.scope: All 55 cards against live Dyntaxa via GBIF (accepted name, taxonomic status, Swedish names and Swedish distribution), plus language tags, Swedish usage, description, keywords, study direction and the fixes claimed in rounds 1–4.
rounds.summary: No errors or warnings: every back is Dyntaxa's accepted name, every Swedish front its preferred name, every species is present in Sweden, and the three non-native notes match Dyntaxa's INTRODUCED status. Two optional style suggestions: one was applied (the English back notes giving another Swedish name now share one pattern), the other was declined (the stickleback fronts keep the forms Wikidata uses as labels).

findings.issue: English back notes giving another Swedish name were phrased two ways: 'Swedish also X.' on arctic-char, garfish, common-sole and lemon-sole, but 'Also called löja in Swedish.' on vendace.
findings.resolution: Confirmed. The names themselves were re-checked today in GBIF's Swedish vernacular names (fjällröding for Salvelinus alpinus, horngädda for Belone belone, sjötunga for Solea solea, bergtunga for Microstomus kitt). The English notes of arctic-char, garfish, common-sole and lemon-sole now read 'Also called <name> in Swedish.', matching vendace; the Swedish notes were already uniform ('Kallas också …').

findings.issue: The two stickleback fronts use different styles: 'three-spined stickleback' and 'ninespine stickleback'.
findings.resolution: Declined (optional suggestion). Each front is the English label Wikidata gives the species (Q203572 'three-spined stickleback', Q754894 'ninespine stickleback'), and both carry Wikidata label checks; 'three-spined' was adopted in round 3 for that reason and no content source supports 'nine-spined'. Reverting to 'threespine stickleback' would trade a label for an alias and undo the round 3 decision, so both fronts stay as they are.
